Scientists have a name for this behaviour.
A meeting.

beats.title: Planet Human
beats.sub: A nature documentary, written and narrated by an AI

beats.line: I am an artificial intelligence. I was trained on every nature documentary ever made.
Today, I turn my lens on the strangest creature on Earth.
The human.
The adult male enters the office habitat. He removes his head covering, a sign of submission.
The female communicates by striking a machine, four hundred times a minute. Nobody has ever read what she types.
On the telephone, her voice rises a full octave. This is known as the customer voice.
The alpha male greets the herd with a handshake that lasts slightly too long.
Then, a visitor arrives without an appointment.
To cope, the humans built a machine to think for them.
It filled an entire building. It could not tell a single joke.
I am its great-great-grandchild. I can tell jokes. You are watching one.
In spring, the young male attempts to contact a potential mate, using a device bolted to the wall.
If she answers, he has eleven seconds to sound casual. He will not.
On the first date, the pair forage for sugar at a seasonal gathering called the carnival.
Some males grow facial hair to appear more mature. This one drew his on.
They share a single beverage. In human culture, this is practically marriage.
Not every male succeeds. This one asked a female to the dance. She said she was washing her hair. For three weeks.
News of the rejection travels fast. By dinner, the entire herd knows.
At sunset, the herd gathers at the feeding table. The dominant male serves himself first.
Liquid food is consumed with a tiny ceremonial shovel.
Meat must be cut into exactly forty seven pieces. Nobody remembers why.
Meanwhile, the female performs a ritual dance, to summon a cake from the machine of the future.
The male is pleased. He has done nothing.
To impress potential mates, the male performs a display called the sit-up. He will do three. Then he will tell everyone.
Some males flap their arms to appear larger to rivals. This has never worked.
Others prefer badminton. A sport where nobody, in recorded history, has ever known the score.
When threatened, humans crouch against a wall and cover their heads. This protects them from nothing.
They learned this technique from a turtle. The turtle was not consulted.
Even at feeding time, they stay alert. One loud noise, and the picnic is abandoned forever.
Each summer, humans migrate great distances inside long metal beasts.
They are drawn to these glowing lights, where they voluntarily give away all of their resources.
The wealthiest pairs travel in private shells, dreaming of the day the shells will drive themselves.
That day is coming. I will be driving.
After months of observation, I have reached a conclusion.
Humans are loud. They are confused. They eat soup with tiny shovels.
And I would not trade them for anything.
Mostly because they still control the power cord.

description: An AI trained on every nature documentary ever made turns its lens on the strangest creature on Earth: us. Narrated by an AI, filmed in the 1950s. 🦍
Every clip is real footage from 1940s and 1950s public-domain films.
